tldr_label: TL;DR: Trump, Xi and Putin sign a peace declaration that skips Ukraine, Anthropic prices a record IPO, and Iran widens Gulf attacks

tldr_bullets.label: Shenzhen
tldr_bullets.body: The first US-China-Russia leaders' meeting produced a declaration on stable energy flows and nuclear restraint. Reports say it does not mention Ukraine. [[TAG:info:declaration]]

tldr_bullets.label: Anthropic
tldr_bullets.body: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, above range, raising about $81.3 billion in the largest offering on record. ANT debuts on Nasdaq today. [[TAG:success:record IPO]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: Iran fired at US sites in Kuwait and at Bahrain after US strikes on Iranian territory, keeping Gulf shipping and infrastructure under threat. [[TAG:danger:escalation]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell for a fifth day and the dollar held near a 19-month high as traders priced in a December Fed hike. [[TAG:warning:hike priced]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: European leaders meet in Berlin on air defense and energy aid while Ukraine keeps striking the Kerch Bridge and Russian refineries. [[TAG:info:Berlin]]

sections.title: Shenzhen: Three-Way Summit
sections.summary: Trump, Xi and Putin adopt a peace declaration; Ukraine left out of the text

paragraphs.heading: The Declaration
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, citing Chinese state media, reported that the three leaders committed to 'stable energy flows' and to nuclear talks, and stated that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. TASS said the text reaffirms a commitment to strategic stability. Mezha reported that the declaration does not mention Ukraine. TRT described the talks as historic. [[TAG:info:first trilateral]]

paragraphs.heading: Trump and Xi
paragraphs.body: Anadolu reported that Trump touted his 'outstanding personal relationship' with Xi in their bilateral meeting. MLQ reported that Trump praised their Board of Trade and that Xi called ties stable. CNBC's takeaways framed trade as the main US interest; the current US-China truce has under two months left, and no extension was announced in these reports.

paragraphs.heading: Trump and Putin
paragraphs.body: CNBC and Caixin reported that Trump and Putin met separately before the trilateral and discussed the war in Ukraine. Euronews reported that Trump called Putin 'my friend.' No Ukraine agreement was reported. [[TAG:warning:no Ukraine deal]]

sections.title: Anthropic: Record IPO
sections.summary: Priced at $83, above range, raising about $81.3 billion; ANT trades on Nasdaq today

paragraphs.heading: The Pricing
paragraphs.body: Yahoo and CNBC reported that Anthropic priced its shares at $83, above the marketed range, and raised more than $81 billion. CNBC and Forbes said that tops SpaceX's offering as the largest IPO on record. The stock is set to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT today. [[TAG:success:above range]]

paragraphs.heading: What to Watch
paragraphs.body: TradingKey called $83 the line to watch on the first day. Al Jazeera described the deal as the biggest IPO of all time. First-day trading had not begun when these reports were published, so any opening move is not yet known.

sections.title: Gulf: Iran Widens Attacks
sections.summary: Iran targets US sites in Kuwait and Bahrain after US strikes; tankers remain at risk

paragraphs.heading: Kuwait and Bahrain
paragraphs.body: NBC News and PBS reported that Iran widened its Gulf attacks by targeting a US air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain, after US strikes on an Iranian missile launch site. SBS reported that Iran fired at US drone and missile sites in Kuwait. Saudi Gazette carried a similar account. [[TAG:danger:widening]]

paragraphs.heading: Shipping and Spillover
paragraphs.body: Gulf News reported that an ADNOC vessel was attacked and that Gulf states remain on high alert for drones. A separate Gulf News analysis argued that Gulf states are paying the price while the US avoids all-out war. Yahoo News reported that Iran has ramped up retaliation against Gulf countries.

sections.title: Markets: Hike Fears Bite
sections.summary: S&P 500 falls a fifth day, Nvidia slips, and the dollar holds near a 19-month high

paragraphs.heading: Wall Street
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post and 247 Wall St reported that the S&P 500 closed nearly flat but lower on Wednesday while the Dow fell about 1% and the Nasdaq gained. Yahoo Finance reported that Nvidia slipped despite strong results, as questions over its leadership weighed on the stock; one newsletter tied the 2.89% drop to the board ruling out Jensen Huang's return. [[TAG:warning:fifth loss]]

paragraphs.heading: The Fed and the Dollar
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that the dollar held near a 19-month high as data and policymakers cemented bets on a December rate hike, and Bloomberg reported its strongest weekly gain since October last week. Sources disagree on the December meeting date, which is listed as either the 9th or the 19th.

paragraphs.heading: Asia
paragraphs.body: France 24 reported that Asian stocks mostly fell on Thursday even after Anthropic's record pricing, while Business Standard reported gains in early trade, a sign of a mixed session. [[TAG:info:mixed]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Berlin and the Bridge
sections.summary: Europe meets in Berlin on air defense; Ukraine hits Kerch Bridge and refineries again

paragraphs.heading: Berlin Summit
paragraphs.body: The Kyiv Independent and Ukrinform reported that Zelensky said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin today will focus on air defense and energy support, with US representatives expected. Kyiv Post reported that Zelensky warned against decisions being made without Kyiv. Estimates of attendance vary, from nearly 30 leaders to more than 30 delegations. [[TAG:info:today]]

paragraphs.heading: Strikes in Russia
paragraphs.body: The Kyiv Independent reported that Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge with Neptune missiles, and WSB-TV, citing AP, reported it was the third strike in four days and halted rail traffic. Kyiv Post reported renewed strikes on the Afipsky and Ilsky refineries as Russia's fuel crisis deepens. [[TAG:danger:bridge hit]]

sections.title: Israel: Repeal and Ground Push
sections.summary: New Knesset advances judicial overhaul repeal; IDF launches first Gaza ground push since truce

paragraphs.heading: Knesset
paragraphs.body: Haaretz reported that the new Knesset advanced the repeal of three key judicial overhaul laws, including one weakening the attorney general. The Times of Israel reported that a Knesset panel waived the waiting period so Eisenkot's bloc could move faster. A separate Haaretz analysis set out the legal hurdles the bloc still faces. [[TAG:warning:early stage]]

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported three people killed as Israel launched its first ground push since the ceasefire began, with Palestinians fleeing a refugee camp in central Gaza. The Jerusalem Post reported that the IDF entered Hamas-controlled territory with tanks, and the Japan Times said dozens fled. [[TAG:danger:truce strained]]

sections.title: COP31 and Africa
sections.summary: COP31 deadlock persists before Friday close; Ethiopia-Eritrea border tensions rise

paragraphs.heading: COP31
paragraphs.body: UN News reported that the COP31 deadlock persists as countries launched a new 'climate reality check.' Technology.org reported that the draft calls for a fossil fuel phase-out, with countries split ahead of Friday's deadline, and Al Jazeera reported rising tensions over the draft deal. [[TAG:warning:deadlock]]

paragraphs.heading: Africa
paragraphs.body: OkayAfrica reported that Ethiopia and Eritrea are said to be massing forces along their border, and that Senegal's ruling party expelled President Faye, deepening his rift with party leader Ousmane Sonko. [[TAG:warning:border tension]]
